title: EIA Open Data API v2 (U.S. Energy Information Administration)
questions: average retail electricity price by state
energy consumption per capita by state
natural gas price for residential customers
CO2 emissions from power plants by state

key_only: more than a handful of requests an hour (without a key the pack uses api.data.gov's DEMO_KEY, which allowed 10 requests an hour from one address when checked)

manual.keyless_citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration, {dataset}, Petroleum & Other Liquids data series history (www.eia.gov/dnav/pet), retrieved {retrieved_long}.
manual.keyless_file: Petroleum series without a key (when DEMO_KEY is rate-limited): EIA's history file https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist_xls/<series><d|w|m|a>.xls (d daily, w weekly, m monthly, a annual; one series per file, 30-500 KB), e.g. EMM_EPMR_PTE_NUS_DPGm.xls (U.S. regular gasoline, monthly), EMD_EPD2D_PTE_NUS_DPGw.xls (diesel, weekly), RWTCd.xls (WTI, daily), MGFUPUS2m.xls (finished motor gasoline product supplied, monthly). Covers a data request of any petroleum/* route that gives facets {"series": [one id]}, no other facet, and the value column; --check lists the exact files in keyless_files. Pass the .xls as downloaded to ingest_command (reading it needs the xlrd package), which keeps the request's dates. Not for electricity, natural gas, SEDS or other routes, or several series in one request.
manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (each returns JSON with up to 5,000 rows; the links carry DEMO_KEY: replace it with your own free key from https://www.eia.gov/opendata/register.php if the hourly limit is hit), save each under the name shown, upload them, then --ingest. Without the bundle: the API browser https://www.eia.gov/opendata/browser/ builds the same query (route, frequency, facets, dates) and downloads CSV or Excel; or the data pages on eia.gov (e.g. Electric Power Monthly, State Energy Data System) have spreadsheets. Upload the file and say which it is.

cache.why: Series are updated weekly to annually and revised; data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: EIA data are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); EIA's copyright and reuse page asks that EIA be cited as the source.

citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration, {dataset}, EIA Open Data API v2 (api.eia.gov), retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Nominal or real (inflation-adjusted) prices? EIA prices are nominal unless the series says otherwise.
Which frequency and sector (residential, commercial, industrial, all sectors)? Averages across sectors mix very different prices.
